A_target.statement:
Any two [[Definition:Countable Set|countable]] [[Definition:Dense Linear Order|dense linear orders]] without endpoints are [[Definition:Order Isomorphism|order isomorphic]].
In particular each is isomorphic to $\struct {\Q, <}$.

B_source.statement:
Let $A$, $B$ be dense linear orders without endpoints and $p$ a finite order-preserving [[Definition:Partial Mapping|partial map]] from $A$ to $B$.
Then for any $a \in A$ there is a finite order-preserving extension of $p$ defined at $a$, and for any $b \in B$ one with $b$ in its range.

substitutions.a single extension step: alternate steps adding elements of A and of B

object_map.reformulation: Approximate the isomorphism by finite partial isomorphisms, alternately extending the domain and the range.

validity_conditions: Density and the absence of endpoints are what make each finite extension possible.
Countability allows every element to be handled at some finite stage.
proof_plan: Enumerate $A = \set {a_0, a_1, \ldots}$ and $B = \set {b_0, b_1, \ldots}$, and let $p_0 = \O$.

At even steps, extend $p_n$ to the first $a_k$ not yet in the domain; at odd steps, extend it to cover the first $b_k$ not yet in the range.
Both are possible by the source result.
$p = \bigcup_n p_n$ is order-preserving, defined on all of $A$, and maps onto $B$.
